review.decision: Keep missing recording baselines and failed counter writes unprovable until fresh authorization
review.notes: R5 independently identified two indistinguishable empty intervals. Test recovery after the first ordinary event, and a temporarily unwritable counter with retained old bytes. Keep stopped recording content-free and verify a genuinely fresh same-action authorization.

cases.description: An uninitialized authority baseline and a failed recording-gap write cannot authorize a stale continuation after recovery.
cases.setup: Isolated real workspace, journal, config and sequence files with original user authority and an exact target.
cases.action: Save an instruction before journal initialization; suppress a target pause and then record an unrelated Stop. Disable recording with a previously initialized counter that cannot be advanced, restore it, and try the old direct source and an explicit new source.
cases.expected: Neither later availability nor an ordinary Stop revives the old authority. Failed counter persistence is observable and the old reference remains unsafe; an explicit newer confirmed step can use the same action once. No disabled event or private input is recorded.
